prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1287; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in Baytown, on the main road heading toward the bridge, in the right lane.
Q: What were you doing right before the impact?
A: I was changing lanes to the left because traffic in the right lane was slowing down. I checked my mirror, I saw a gap, and I started to move over.
Q: Did you use your turn signal?
A: Yes, I'm pretty sure I had it on for a few seconds before I moved.
Q: What happened next?
A: Then I felt a bang on my driver's side. The other car had come up in my blind spot and clipped the side of my vehicle. It pushed me toward the median and I had to fight the wheel to get stopped.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the contact?
A: No. I didn't see it until it was right beside me.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. I put my left hand out to brace myself against the steering wheel and the door frame, and my wrist hurt right away. I went to the emergency room later that day and they told me it's a fracture. I've got a cast on it now.
Q: Did you need any further treatment?
A: I've been told I may need a follow-up with an orthopedic specialist, and I'm waiting on that appointment.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident?
A: Only that the other driver seemed to be going fast. That's my impression, but I'd leave that for the police report to confirm.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
